headline: High risk of cascading automation errors and data leakage; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are moderate due to shared file/network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra reads/writes files and can pass workflow outputs through stdin/stdout and APIs, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can consume upstream content. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled document text influence downstream workflow logic. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from the profiles.
conditions: IF Kestra ingests PaddleOCR output from a shared file or API response without sanitization
IF PaddleOCR processes attacker-supplied documents that Kestra later treats as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict content/schema validator between OCR output and workflow steps
Separate input and control files into different directories
Disable automatic execution of text extracted from documents
Log and review any workflow step that consumes OCR output
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from OCR output to downstream tasks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. PaddleOCR processes documents and images and has allowlisted egress. If sensitive documents flow from Kestra into OCR, either agent may expose content through logs or outbound API calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF Kestra passes sensitive documents or artifacts to PaddleOCR
IF either agent logs raw document contents or OCR text
IF PaddleOCR sends extracted content to an external API on its allowlist
mitigations: Redact secrets before OCR ingestion
Turn off verbose logging for both agents
Restrict OCR inputs to non-sensitive documents
Review outbound allowlist entries for data exfiltration risk
requires-engineering: add field-level DLP on workflow artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and request root/docker.sock, while PaddleOCR runs browsers and has API egress. If both operate on the same workspace or shared mutable files, they can overwrite each other's artifacts or race on outputs. No locking or isolation between them is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact store
IF Kestra launches subprocesses that modify files PaddleOCR is reading
IF the orchestrator does not provide per-agent locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Run each agent under distinct OS users
Make outputs immutable before handoff
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, notifications, and downstream actions, and PaddleOCR can transform documents into text that Kestra may consume. If Kestra treats OCR output as authoritative, a recognition error can cascade into emails, PagerDuty alerts, or cloud actions. The default automation surface makes this dangerous without explicit verification.
conditions: IF Kestra routes PaddleOCR output into notification or action tasks
IF no human or rule-based verification occurs before downstream execution
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action task
Require confidence thresholds for OCR-derived fields
Route uncertain extractions to manual review
Disable auto-remediation on first-pass OCR results
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between OCR and workflow steps

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra handles logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If those documents contain regulated personal data, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through workflow logs or external API calls. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the safest reading is a medium compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is included in documents processed by PaddleOCR
IF Kestra retains logs or artifacts longer than the source policy
IF OCR output is sent to a region or vendor without a matching DPA
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from OCR jobs
Set short retention on workflow logs and artifacts
Confirm residency and DPA coverage for outbound OCR calls
Mask personal data before storage
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention enforcement
